headings: Our Principal Services and Regions of Operation
paragraphs: Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. (together with its subsidiaries, "Cushman & Wakefield," "the Company," "we," "ours" and "us") is a leading global commercial real estate services firm driven to solve complex problems for real estate occupiers and investors. Led by an experienced executive team, our approximately 53,000 employees in over 350 offices and nearly 60 countries provide exceptional problem-solving, advisory and execution across the built environment, and manage approximately 6.5 billion square feet of commercial real estate globally. Our business is focused on meeting the increasing demands of our clients through comprehensive global offerings including (i) Services, (ii) Leasing, (iii) Capital markets and (iv) Valuation and other services. In 2025, 2024 and 2023, we generated revenues of $10.3 billion, $9.4 billion and $9.5 billion, respectively.

Since 2014, we have built a company with the scale and global footprint to effectively serve our multinational and local clients' needs. Today, Cushman & Wakefield is one of the top three real estate services providers as measured by revenue and workforce. We have gained third-party recognition as a provider and employer of choice, having consistently been named in the top four in our industry's leading brand study, the Lipsey Company's Top 25 Commercial Real Estate Brands, and a leading global outsourcing service provider by the International Association of Outsourcing Professionals.

We are a firm built around the belief that Better never settles. As an organization and as individuals, we will never settle for the world that's been built, but relentlessly drive it forward for our clients, colleagues and communities. Our core values (Driven, Resilient, Inclusive, Visionary and Entrepreneurial) drive our business, create inspiration and help us provide value-added services to the built environment every day.

We have built an integrated and scalable platform that we believe is well positioned to support our growth strategy by focusing on providing effective problem solving through quality advice and execution, continuing to operate with rigor, investing in advanced technologies and innovative practices, and recruiting, developing and retaining top talent.

Our global presence and integrated platform enable us to provide a broad base of services across geographies. This global footprint, complemented by a full suite of service offerings, positions us as one of a small number of firms able to provide solutions to complex global mandates from large multinational occupiers and investors.

Our business is organized, and we report our operating results, through three geographic segments: the Americas; Europe, Middle East and Africa ("EMEA"); and Asia Pacific ("APAC") representing 73%, 10% and 17% of our 2025 total revenue and 71%, 13% and 16% of our 2025 service line fee revenue, respectively. We operate the following service lines within each of our segments: (i) Services, (ii) Leasing, (iii) Capital markets and (iv) Valuation and other, representing 66%, 21%, 8% and 5% of our 2025 revenue, respectively, and 51%, 30%, 12% and 7% of our 2025 service line fee revenue, respectively.

By revenue, our largest country was the United States, representing 69%, 71% and 72% of revenue in the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, followed by Australia, representing 5% of revenue in each of the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Services. Our largest service line based on revenue includes property management, facilities management, facilities services and project management services. Revenues in this service line are generally recurring in nature, many through multi-year contracts with relatively high switching costs.

For real estate occupiers, we offer integrated facilities management, portfolio administration, transaction management and strategic consulting. These services are offered individually or through our global occupier services offering, which provides a comprehensive range of bundled services resulting in consistent quality of service and cost savings.

For real estate investors, we offer a variety of property management services, which include client accounting, engineering and operations, lease administration, tenant experience and residential property management.

In addition, we offer globally to both occupiers and investors (i) self-performed facilities services, which include janitorial, maintenance, critical environment management, landscaping and office services, (ii) project management, (iii) workplace consulting and (iv) sustainability services.

Fees in this service line are generally based on a fixed recurring fee or a variable fee, which may be based on hours incurred, a percentage mark-up on actual costs incurred or a percentage of monthly gross receipts. Additionally, this service line has a large component of revenue that consists of us contracting with third-party providers (engineers, landscapers, etc.) and then passing these expenses on to our clients.

Leasing. Our second largest service line based on revenue, Leasing, consists of two primary sub-services: owner representation and tenant representation. In owner representation leasing, we typically contract with a building owner on a multi-month or multi-year agreement to provide strategic advice and execution to lease their available space. In tenant representation leasing, we are typically engaged by a tenant to identify and negotiate a lease for them in the form of a renewal, expansion or relocation, or occasionally to enter into a sublease or lease termination if they desire space reduction. We have a higher degree of visibility into Leasing services fees due to contractual renewal dates, leading to renewal, expansion or new lease revenue. In addition, Leasing fees can be somewhat less cyclical as many tenants need to renew or lease space to operate even in difficult economic conditions.
Leasing fees are typically earned after a lease is signed and are calculated as a percentage of the total value of rent payable over the life of the lease.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
Sociopolitical polarization and changes in political landscapes may pose risks to our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our operations are subject to social, geopolitical and economic risks in different countries.
Our operations are subject to foreign currency volatility.
Significant portions of our revenue and cash flow are seasonal, which could cause our results of operations and liquidity to fluctuate significantly.
Our success depends upon our ability to recruit and retain qualified revenue-producing advisors and senior management.
Failure to maintain and execute information technology strategies could materially and adversely affect our ability to remain competitive in the market.
A security breach or other threat relating to our information systems could lead to confidential information being exposed which could increase the risk of liability and damage our reputation.
The concentration of business with specific corporate clients can increase business risk, and our business can be adversely affected by a loss of certain of these clients.
Our brand and reputation are key assets of our company and will be affected by how we are perceived in the marketplace.
Infrastructure disruptions may impede our ability to manage real estate for clients.
Our historical growth has benefited from mergers, acquisitions and investments, which may not perform as expected, and similar opportunities may not be available in the future.
Our goodwill or our equity method investments could become impaired, which may require us to take significant non-cash charges against earnings.
Exposure to additional tax liabilities stemming from our global operations, as well as changes in tax legislation or tax rates, could adversely affect our financial results.
Bermuda's limited network of international tax treaties may present an incremental tax risk.
A failure by third parties to comply with contractual, regulatory or legal requirements could result in economic or reputational harm to us.
We face risks related to climate change, including physical and transition risks, and with respect to other environmental conditions.
The agreements governing our indebtedness impose certain operating and financial restrictions on us, and in an event of a default, all such indebtedness could become immediately due and payable.
Our amount of indebtedness may adversely affect our available cash flow and our ability to operate our business, remain in compliance with our debt covenants and make payments on our indebtedness.
Despite our current indebtedness levels, we and our subsidiaries may still be able to incur more indebtedness, which could further exacerbate the risks associated with our leverage.
We are subject to various litigation and regulatory risks and may face financial liabilities and/or damage to our reputation as a result of litigation.
paragraphs: An investment in our common shares involves risks and uncertainty, including, but not limited to, the risk factors described below. If any of the risks described below actually occur, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below as well as our audited consolidated financial statements and the related notes ("Consolidated Financial Statements"), when evaluating the information contained in this Annual Report.

Our business is significantly impacted by general macroeconomic conditions and global and regional demand for commercial real estate and, accordingly, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be materially adversely affected by market conditions or macroeconomic challenges.

Demand for our services is largely dependent on the relative strength of the global and regional commercial real estate markets, which are highly sensitive to general macroeconomic conditions. Macroeconomic uncertainty continued in many markets around the world in 2025, including factors such as elevated inflation, international trade policy and new or elevated tariffs, elevated levels of unemployment, changes in interest rates and volatility in foreign currency exchange rates, among other macroeconomic challenges. These factors have in the past, and may in the future, negatively impact our business, and can lead to ongoing volatility within global capital and credit markets and cause delays in certain real estate transaction decisions.

In particular, some of our clients continued to face challenges when attempting to procure credit or financing in 2025 due to challenging lending conditions and higher capital costs. Clients have in the past and may continue in the future to delay real estate transaction decisions until property values and economic conditions further stabilize, or the economic recovery may progress more slowly than we expect, which could continue to reduce the commissions and fees we earn for brokering those transactions. Furthermore, the continuing prevalence of hybrid working models in certain geographies or industries has resulted in structural changes to the utilization of many types of commercial real estate, which could have ongoing repercussions for our business. A delay or stall in any economic recovery, any future uncertainty, weakness or volatility in the credit markets, a decline in the U.S. or global economy, or the public perception that any of these events may occur, could further affect global and regional demand for commercial real estate, which would negatively affect the performance of some or all of our service lines and our overall business, financial conditions and results of operations.

The increasing division and polarization of political ideologies, both in the United States and internationally, could negatively impact our operations. Changes in political landscapes, including changes in government leadership or policy priorities, may result in shifts in legal, regulatory or policy frameworks, which in turn may increase our costs, result in labor challenges, require us to quickly adapt our business practices or result in decreased competitiveness. Political polarization can also influence client behavior and perceptions. If we or our management team are perceived as aligned with a particular political ideology, it may negatively affect our reputation, brand and ability to attract or retain certain clients. Conflicting political ideologies could also lead to workplace challenges, including increased tensions or reduced collaboration, making it more difficult for us to attract or retain key personnel. Additionally, heightened political polarization could escalate into social or civil unrest, posing risks to personnel safety or disrupting our operations. Such unrest could also lead to economic instability and cause unpredictable market conditions that could adversely affect demand for our services and our results of operations, as discussed in further detail above.

We conduct a significant portion of our business and employ a substantial number of people outside of the United States and, as a result, we are subject to risks associated with doing business globally. Our international operations expose us to international economic trends as well as foreign government policy measures. paragraphs: On November 27, 2025, we completed a court-approved scheme of arrangement in the U.K., pursuant to which a new Bermudan holding company, Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. became the sole shareholder of Cushman & Wakefield plc and the parent company of the entire group of Cushman & Wakefield companies (the "Redomiciliation"). The Redomiciliation resulted in the Cushman & Wakefield group parent company changing its jurisdiction of incorporation from England and Wales to Bermuda. This transaction has not and is not expected to have any material change on our day-to-day operations.
•Revenue of $10.3 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased 9% from the year ended December 31, 2024.
◦Services revenue increased 4% (or 6% excluding the impact of the sale of a non-core Services business in August 2024), reflecting continued momentum across all segments.
◦Leasing revenue increased 8%, driven primarily by office and industrial leasing in the Americas.
◦Capital markets revenue increased 19%, with strong performance across all segments and asset classes.
◦Valuation and other revenue increased 9%.

•Net income of $88.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $43.1 million from the year ended December 31, 2024. Diluted earnings per share for 2025 was $0.38 compared to $0.56 for 2024.
◦Recognized a one-time other-than-temporary impairment loss of $177.0 million on our investment in the Greystone JV.
◦Adjusted EBITDA (as defined below) of $656.2 million increased 13% from the year ended December 31, 2024.
•Net cash provided by operating activities of $340.4 million for 2025 increased $132.4 million from 2024.

•In 2025, we completed three repricings of our Term Loans due in 2030, achieving the lowest credit spread in the Company's history. We also elected to prepay $300.0 million in principal outstanding under the Company's Term Loans.
•Liquidity as of December 31, 2025 was $1.8 billion, consisting of availability on the Company's undrawn revolving credit facility of $1.0 billion and cash and cash equivalents of $0.8 billion.

paragraphs: Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. （含其子公司在內，"Cushman & Wakefield"、"the Company"、"we"、"ours" 以及 "us"）為全球知名的商業不動產服務公司，致力於為不動產使用人與投資人解決複雜問題。由經驗豐富的高階管理團隊領導，我們約有 53,000 名員工，在超過 350 個辦公室與近 60 個國家提供卓越的問題解決、諮詢與執行服務，並管理約 6.5 十億平方英呎的全球商業不動產。我們的業務聚焦於透過全面的全球服務方案，回應客戶日益增長的需求，包括（i）服務、（ii）租賃、（iii）資本市場以及（iv）評估及其他服務。2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年，我們分別產生了 10.3 十億美元、9.4 十億美元及 9.5 十億美元的營業收入。

自 2014 年以來，我們已建立了一家規模與全球版圖足以有效服務我們多國及本地客戶需求的公司。目前，Cushman & Wakefield 為全球前三大不動產服務提供商之一，以營業收入及員工數量為衡量標準。我們已獲得第三方認可為優秀的服務提供商及僱主，持續被列為產業領先品牌研究 "Lipsey 公司的 Top 25 商業不動產品牌" 中的前四名，並被國際外包專業協會認可為領先的全球外包服務提供商。
我們是一家秉持 "Better never settles" 信念的公司。作為組織及個人，我們從不滿足於現有的世界，而是持續為客戶、同事及社區推動進步。我們的核心價值觀（驅動、韌性、包容、遠見及創業精神）推動我們的業務，創造靈感，並幫助我們每天為建築環境提供增值服務。
我們已建立一個整合且可擴展的平台，我們相信這個平台能有效支持我們的成長策略，透過提供高品質的建議與執行，解決問題，持續以嚴謹的作風運作，投資先進科技與創新實踐，並招募、培訓及留住頂尖人才。
我們的全球佈局與整合平台使我們能為不同地區的客戶提供廣泛的服務。這個全球版圖，搭配完整的服務方案，使我們成為少數能為大型多國使用人及投資人解決複雜全球任務的公司之一。

我們的業務依地理區域進行組織，並透過三個地理分部報告營運成果：美洲；歐洲、中東及非洲（"EMEA"）；以及亞太（"APAC"），分別佔我們 2025 年總營業收入的 73%、10% 和 17%，以及 2025 年服務線費用收入的 71%、13% 和 16%。我們在每個分部內提供以下服務線：（i）服務、（ii）租賃、（iii）資本市場及（iv）評估及其他，分別佔我們 2025 年營業收入的 66%、21%、8% 和 5%，以及 2025 年服務線費用收入的 51%、30%、12% 和 7%。
按營業收入計算，我們最大的國家為美國，分別佔 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年、2024 年 12 月 31 日財年及 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年的營業收入 69%、71% 和 72%，其後為澳洲，分別佔 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年、2024 年 12 月 31 日財年及 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年的營業收入 5%。
服務。我們最大的服務線（按營業收入計算）包括不動產管理、設施管理、設施服務及專案管理服務。此服務線的收入通常為持續性收入，許多透過多年期合約，且轉換成本相對較高。
對於不動產使用人，我們提供整合性設施管理、資產管理、交易管理及策略諮詢服務。這些服務可個別提供，或透過我們的全球不動產使用人服務方案，提供一整套組合服務，以確保服務品質一致且節省成本。
對於不動產投資人，我們提供多樣化的不動產管理服務，包括客戶會計、工程與運作、租賃管理、租戶體驗及住宅不動產管理。
此外，我們針對不動產使用人與投資人提供全球性服務，包括（i）自行執行的設施服務，包含清潔、維護、關鍵環境管理、園藝及辦公室服務，（ii）專案管理，（iii）工作場所諮詢及（iv）永續服務。
此服務線的費用通常基於固定重複費用或變動費用，變動費用可能根據實際耗用小時數、實際成本的百分比 markup 或每月毛收入的百分比計算。此外，此服務線包含大量收入來自我們與第三方服務提供者（如工程師、園藝師等）簽約，並將這些費用轉嫁給客戶。

租賃。根據營業收入計算，這是我們第二大的服務線，租賃服務包含兩個主要子服務：所有者代表租賃與租戶代表租賃。在所有者代表租賃中，我們通常與大樓所有者簽訂多個月或多年的契約，為其提供戰略建議與執行，以租賃其可用空間。在租戶代表租賃中，我們通常被租戶聘請，以協助其尋找並協議租賃，形式為續約、擴張或遷移，偶爾也會協助其簽訂次租賃或終止租賃，以減少所需空間。我們對租賃服務費用有較高的可見度，因契約續約日期導致續約、擴張或新租賃收入。此外，租賃費用可能較少受到總體經濟週期的影響，因為許多租戶即使在困難的經濟條件下仍需續約或租賃空間以維持營運。
租賃費用通常在租賃協議簽訂後產生，並以租賃期間總租金價值的百分比計算。

paragraphs: 於 2025 年 11 月 27 日，我們完成英國法院批准的公司重整方案，根據該方案，一間新設於百慕達的控股公司 Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. 成為 Cushman & Wakefield plc 唯一股東，並成為 Cushman & Wakefield 全體公司的母公司（以下稱為「重 domiciliation」）。重 domiciliation 使 Cushman & Wakefield 羣體母公司將其註冊地從英格蘭及威爾斯變更為百慕達。此交易對我們的日常營運並未產生且預期也將不會產生重大影響。
• 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年營業收入為 10.3 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年成長 9%。
◦ 服務收入成長 4%（或排除 2024 年 8 月出售非核心服務業務影響後成長 6%），反映各應報告分部持續成長動能。
◦ 租賃收入成長 8%，主要由美洲地區辦公室及工業租賃所驅動。
◦ 資本市場收入成長 19%，各應報告分部及資產類別表現強勁。
◦ 評估及其他收入成長 9%。
• 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年淨收入為 88.2 百萬美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年減少 43.1 百萬美元。2025 年每股稀釋後盈餘為 0.38 美元，較 2024 年 0.56 美元為低。
◦ 認列一筆一次性非暫時性減值損失 177.0 百萬美元，係針對我們在 Greystone 聯合企業之投資。
◦調整後營業現金流量（定義如下）為 656.2 百萬美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年成長 13%。
•2025 年營運活動所提供之淨現金為 340.4 百萬美元，較 2024 年增加 132.4 百萬美元。
•2025 年，本公司完成三筆到期日為 2030 年的定期貸款重 pricing，達成本公司歷史上最低的信用利差。本公司亦選擇提前償還 300.0 百萬美元本金，為本公司定期貸款所欠本金。
•2025 年 12 月 31 日流動性為 1.8 十億美元，包含本公司未動用循環信貸融資之可用額 1.0 十億美元，以及現金及現金等價物 0.8 十億美元。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
社會政治極化及政治版圖之變動可能對我們之業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成風險。
我們之營運面臨不同國家之社會、地緣政治及經濟風險。
我們之營運面臨外幣波動之風險。
我們之營收及現金流有相當大之部分具季節性，這可能會導致我們之營運成果及流動性產生顯著波動。
我們之成功取決於我們招募並留住具備營收能力之顧問及高階管理階層之能力。
未能維持並執行資訊科技策略，可能會對我們在市場中保持競爭力之能力造成重大且不利之影響。
資訊系統遭駭客入侵或其他威脅，可能會導致機密資訊外洩，進而增加我們之責任風險並損害我們之聲譽。
與特定企業客戶的業務集中度可能增加業務風險，且我們的業務可能因失去其中某些客戶而受到不利影響。
我們的品牌與聲譽是本公司的重要資產，將受到市場對我們看法的影響。
基礎建設中斷可能影響我們管理客戶不動產的能力。
我們的歷史成長受益於併購與投資，這些活動可能未達預期表現，且未來類似機會可能無法取得。
我們的商譽或權益法投資可能發生減值，這可能導致我們必須針對獲利提列重大非現金費用。
因全球業務而產生的額外稅務負擔，以及稅務法規或稅率的變動，可能對我們的財務結果造成不利影響。
百慕達有限的國際稅務條約網路可能帶來額外的稅務風險。
第三方未能遵守契約、法規或法律要求，可能導致我們遭受經濟或聲譽上的損失。
我們面臨與氣候變遷相關的風險，包括實體風險與過渡風險，以及與其他環境條件相關的風險。
與我們負債相關的風險
我們負債的相關協議對我們的營運與財務設有某些限制，若發生違約情況，所有此類負債可能立即成為應償付的現金負債。
我們的負債金額可能不利於我們的現金流量，並影響我們經營業務、符合我們的債務契約條件以及償還負債的能力。
儘管我們目前的負債水準，我們與我們的子公司仍可能繼續發行更多負債，這可能會進一步加劇與我們槓桿相關的風險。
我們面臨各種訴訟與法規風險，並可能因訴訟而面臨財務負擔與/或聲譽受損的後果。

本公司業務受到總體經濟條件及全球與區域商業不動產需求的重大影響，因此，本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況可能因市場條件或總體經濟挑戰而受到重大不利影響。

對我們服務的需求 largely 取決於全球與區域商業不動產市場的相對強度，而這些市場對總體經濟條件極為敏感。2025 年，全球許多市場持續面臨總體經濟不確定性，包括高通貨膨脹、國際貿易政策與新或提高的關稅、失業率高、利率變動及外幣交換率波動等因素，以及其他總體經濟挑戰。這些因素過去曾對本公司業務造成負面影響，未來也可能繼續造成負面影響，並導致全球資本與信貸市場持續波動，並延遲某些不動產交易決策。

特別是，部分客戶在 2025 年因貸款條件嚴峻及資本成本提高，持續面臨取得信貸或融資的困難。客戶過去曾且可能未來繼續延後不動產交易決策，直到房地產價值與經濟條件進一步穩定，或經濟復甦進展不如預期，這可能會繼續減少我們透過促成這些交易所賺取的佣金與費用。此外，某些地理區域或產業中混合工作模式的持續盛行，已導致許多類型商業不動產的使用率產生結構性變動，這可能會對本公司業務產生持續性影響。任何經濟復甦的延遲或停滯、未來任何不確定性、弱勢或波動的信貸市場、美國或全球經濟的衰退，或公眾認為這些事件可能發生的觀感，都可能進一步影響全球與區域商業不動產需求，這將對本公司部分或全部服務線路及整體業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生負面影響，如上文進一步詳述。

美國與國際間政治理念的日益分裂與極化，可能對本公司營運造成負面影響。政治風景的變化，包括政府領導層或政策優先順序的變化，可能導致法律、法規或政策架構的變化，這可能增加本公司成本、導致勞動力挑戰、迫使本公司迅速調整營運作法，或導致本公司競爭力下降。政治極化也可能影響客戶行為與觀感。若本公司或管理團隊被視為與某種政治理念有聯繫，可能對本公司聲譽、品牌及吸引或留住特定客戶的能力造成負面影響。衝突的政治理念也可能導致工作場所的挑戰，包括增加緊張關係或減少合作，使本公司更難吸引或留住關鍵人才。此外，政治極化程度的提高可能升級為社會或民事動亂，對員工安全造成風險或幹擾本公司營運。這種動亂也可能導致經濟不穩定，並造成不可預測的市場條件，這可能會對本公司服務需求及營運成果產生負面影響，如上文進一步詳述。
